prompt: Illustration painted and inked BY HAND on a wood panel — visible wood grain, matte paint, LOOSE HAND-DRAWN PEN HATCHING with natural wobble, rich pen texture on every surface. Storybook, illustrative, imperfect, NOT crisp vector, NOT flat digital. High contrast, generous empty space. Palette strictly: pale bone-grey painted ground, FLAT solid black, white line, ONE accent of glowing BIOLUMINESCENT GREEN. Small black creatures with curled spiral fiddlehead ears and glowing green eyes. NO human figures, NO ordinary cottages, NO pitched-roof cabins, NO doors or windows of human design. No text, no lettering. The dwellings of this world are SPIRAL SHELLS: low coiled walls of stacked volcanic stone that spiral inward like a fern frond or a snail shell, roofed over the coils with salvaged corrugated sheet and fern thatch, entered at the open mouth of the spiral. At the very centre of each spiral, GLOWING BIOLUMINESCENT GREEN light rises from a tapped vein in the ground — the reason the dwelling is there. Close three-quarter view of ONE such spiral dwelling: stacked pale volcanic stone drawn in loose hatching, basalt column posts, ash-clay packed joints, green light spilling up out of its heart, one small black creature with spiral ears sitting at the mouth. Vast empty plain behind, flat black sky.
